subject: mass-communication
title: Model Question Paper 3
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 80 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
For the Optional Modules, attempt Module A (Traditional Media) or Module B (Photojournalism) in the sections that have both.

MCQs carry 1 mark; objective questions carry 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each); very short answers carry 2 marks (30–50 words); short answers 3 marks (50–80 words); the long answer 4 marks (80–120 words).
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.answer: (a) False – the Station Director does. (b) True.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Why are street theatre and comics used for development communication?
questions.answer: They are participatory, in local language and culture and explain sensitive topics simply, e.g. hygiene and HIV/AIDS.

questions.q: Mention any two unhealthy trends in the newspaper industry.
questions.answer: Predatory price wars and excessive dependence on advertisement revenue (also media trials and gifts).

questions.q: Name the three tiers of AIR's broadcasting.
Name any two categories of television channels with an example of each.
questions.answer: News channels – Aaj Tak; sports channels – ESPN (also cartoon – Pogo).

questions.q: Define public relations.
questions.answer: A form of communication used to persuade or influence people by ethical means through two-way communication between an organisation and its public.

sections.title: Optional Module A (Traditional Media): attempt A or Module B. Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Mention any two advantages of traditional media.
questions.answer: They are cost effective and flexible to accommodate new themes; also local, live, with immediate feedback and need no special training.

questions.q: Explain street theatre and its application.
questions.answer: Street theatre combines traditional theatre forms and can be staged anywhere; it uses songs, drama and music to spread messages on child labour, environment, health and women.

sections.title: Optional Module B (Photojournalism): attempt B or Module A. Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is spot news photojournalism?
questions.answer: Covering events that make day-to-day news such as political events, crime and accidents; the most common and demanding type.

questions.q: Discuss any two qualities of a photojournalist.
questions.answer: Alertness and readiness to act fast with the camera at hand; patience and winning the trust of people; truthfulness.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the functions of mass communication.
questions.answer: It informs through news, educates through talks and campaigns (Green Revolution, polio), and entertains through films, serials and music.

questions.q: Discuss the importance of timeliness, proximity and impact in news value.
questions.answer: Timeliness: news must be new (previous day for a paper, every second for a news channel). Proximity: events near us matter more (bird flu in West Bengal). Impact: events affecting many people are big news (the tsunami).

questions.q: Briefly discuss any three limitations of radio broadcast.
questions.answer: It is a one-chance medium as the spoken word is momentary; it has no visual images so is less convincing than television; and messages are easily forgotten.

questions.q: Discuss any two positive and two negative impacts of television.
questions.answer: Positive: education and awareness. Negative: violence and aggression in children; stereotypes and consumerism (also couch potato and obesity).

questions.q: Compare live and recorded programmes.
questions.answer: Live programmes generate excitement and can be made speedily but depend on the crew's performance; recorded programmes allow retakes and editing and market better but lack excitement.

questions.q: What is a website? Write any two features of a website.
questions.answer: A website is the standard new media product, a set of web pages of an organisation or person; features: contact us section with phone and e-mail, news and blogs for feedback, online services.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the business opportunities of new media.
questions.answer: New media ventures are SMEs needing creativity, e.g. niche websites, e-learning, tourism and online shopping, earning through advertising, subscriptions, content selling and services.

sections.title: Optional Module A (Traditional Media): attempt A or Module B. Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Compare traditional media with electronic media.
questions.answer: Traditional media are local, live, intimate, flexible and cost effective but limited in reach and archiving; electronic media reach large heterogeneous audiences instantly with recording but are expensive, less intimate and slow in feedback.

sections.title: Optional Module B (Photojournalism): attempt B or Module A. Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Briefly discuss the points of consideration of the photo editor for selecting a picture in a newspaper.
questions.answer: The major news events of the day (a picture that enhances the lead story), the hard-hitting nature of the picture that tells a story, and reader interest such as local events.
